14th [[Principal Staff Officer (Bangladesh)|Principal Staff Officer of Armed Forces Division]] | president = [[Abdul Hamid (politician)|Abdul Hamid]] | primeminister = [[Sheikh Hasina]] | predecessor = [[Md Mahfuzur Rahman]] | successor = | term_start = 24 November 2020 | term_end = | name = Waker-uz-Zaman | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1966|09|16|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Sherpur District]], [[Pakistan]] | nationality = [[Bangladesh]]i | alma_mater = [[Defence Services Command and Staff College (Bangladesh)|Defence Services Command and Staff College]] {{center|'''Military Training'''
}} [[Bangladesh Military Academy]] | allegiance = {{BAN}} | branch = {{flagicon image|Flag of the Bangladesh Army.svg}} [[Bangladesh Army]] | serviceyears = 1985–present | rank = [[File:Bangladesh-army-OF-8.svg|20px]] [[Lieutenant general]]
[[File:BD Army Lieutenant General Star Plate.svg|40px]] | unit = [[East Bengal Regiment]] | commands = PSO [[Armed Forces Division]], GOC of [[9th Infantry Division (Bangladesh)|9th Infantry Division]] | awards = Army Medal of Glory (SGP) }} '''Waker-uz-Zaman''' ({{lang-bn|ওয়াকার-উজ-জামান}}; born 16 September 1966) is a lieutenant general of the [[Bangladesh Army]] and [[Principal Staff Officer (Bangladesh)|principal staff officer]] of the Prime Minister's Office, [[Armed Forces Division]].{{Cite web|title=Lieutenant General Wakar made PSO|url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/123030/lieutenant-general-wakar-made-pso|access-date=3 November 2021|website=New Age {{!}} The Most Popular Outspoken English Daily in Bangladesh|language=en}} == Early life and education == Zaman graduated from [[Defence Services Command and Staff College (Bangladesh)|Defence Services Command and Staff College]]. He studied at the [[Joint Services Command and Staff College]] in the United Kingdom.{{Cite web|title=General Waqar-uz-Zaman promoted, made PSO at Armed Forces Division|url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2020/11/24/general-waqar-uz-zaman-promoted-made-pso-at-armed-forces-division|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=31 December 2020|website=bdnews24.com}} He holds a master's degree in defence studies from Bangladesh and a Master of Arts in defence studies from King's College, University of London.{{Cite web|title=Principal Staff Officer (PSO), AFD {{!}} Armed Forces Division(AFD)|url=https://afd.gov.bd/pso-afd|access-date=4 November 2021|website=afd.gov.bd}} == Career == Zaman received his commission in 1985 from Bangladesh Military Academy with 13th BMA Long Course at the East Bengal Regiment of Bangladesh Army. Zaman taught at the Non-Commissioned Officer's Academy, [[School of Infantry and Tactics]] and [[Bangladesh Institute of Peace Support Operation Training]]. He served in the [[United Nations Mission in Liberia]] and [[United Nations Angola Verification Mission I]]. He served as Deputy Assistant Military Secretary, Assistant Military Secretary & Deputy Military Secretary in Military Secretary's Branch, Army Headquarters. He served in Army Security Unit & Commanded the 17th East Bengal Regiment. He commanded the 46th Independent Infantry Brigade in Dhaka. Zaman was appointed as Military Secretary of Bangladesh Army in Army Headquarters twice in 2013 and 2017 subsequently. After that he was appointed at 9th Infantry Division as General Officer Commanding (GOC) and Area Commander of Savar Area.{{Cite web|last=Nation|first=The New|title=GOC of Ninth Infantry Division and Commander of Savar Area Major General Waqar-uz-Zaman handing over the championship trophy to Savar Area team, which emerged the champions of the Bangladesh Army Hockey Competition at the Savar Cantonment on Thursday.|url=http://thedailynewnation.com/news/45335/goc-of-ninth-infantry-division-and-commander-of-savar-area-major-general-waqar-uz-zaman-handing-over-the-championship-trophy-to-savar-area-team-which-emerged-the-champions-of-the-bangladesh-army-hockey-competition-at-the-savar-cantonment-on-thursday.html|access-date=3 November 2021|website=The New Nation|language=en}} On 30 November 2020, Zaman was promoted to Lieutenant General and appointed [[Principal Staff Officer (Bangladesh)|Principal Staff Officer]] of [[Armed Forces Division]].{{Cite web|date=30 November 2020|title=New PSO adorned with Lieutenant General rank badge|url=https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2020/11/30/new-pso-adorned-with-lieutenant-general-rank-badge|access-date=31 December 2020|website=Dhaka Tribune}} He is the current chairperson of [[Bangladesh National Authority for Chemical Weapons Convention]].{{Cite web|title=Honorable Chairman|url=http://www.bnacwcafd.gov.bd/menu/chairman|access-date=31 December 2020|website=www.bnacwcafd.gov.bd}} He is a member of the governing body of the [[National Defence College (Bangladesh)|National Defence College]].{{Cite web|title=National Defence College|url=https://www.ndc.gov.bd/Page/GoverningBody|access-date=31 December 2020|website=www.ndc.gov.bd}} == Personal life == Zaman is married to Begum Sarahnaz Kamalika Zaman and the couple have two daughters. He is the son-in-law of late [[General Mustafizur Rahman]], who served as the army chief from 24 December 1997, to 23 December 2000.{{Cite web|title=Lieutenant General Wakar made PSO|url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/123030/lieutenant-general-wakar-made-pso|access-date=4 November 2021|website=New Age {{!}} The Most Popular Outspoken English Daily in Bangladesh|language=en}} == References == {{Reflist|30em}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Zaman}} [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Bangladesh Army generals]] [[Category:Principal Staff Officers (Bangladesh)]] [[Category:1966 births]] [[Category:National Defence College (Bangladesh) alumni]]
